question.problem: A restaurant originally had enough capacity to serve $80$ customers. Following a renovation, the restaurant increased its capacity to $120%$ of the original. What was the capacity of the restaurant after the renovation?
question.worked_solution:
To solve this problem, we can use the formula:

$$
\text{part}=\text{percentage}\times \text{whole}
$$

In our case, the whole is the original number of customers the restaurant was able to receive, which is $80$ customers. The percentage is $120%,$ and the part is the number of customers the restaurant can receive after the renovation.

**Method 1**

First, we convert the percentage to a decimal:

$$
120%=120÷100=1.2
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =120%\times 80 \\  & =1.2\times 80 \\  & =96\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $120%$ of $80$ is $96.$ So, the restaurant can receive $96$ customers after the renovation.

**Method 2**

First, we convert the percentage to a fraction:

$$
120%=\frac{120}{100}=\frac{120÷20}{100÷20}=\frac{6}{5}
$$

Applying our formula, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{part} & =\text{percentage}\times \text{whole} \\  & =120%\times 80 \\  & =\frac{6}{5}\times 80 \\  & =6\times \frac{80}{5} \\  & =6\times 16 \\  & =96\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $120%$ of $80$ is $96.$ So, the restaurant can receive $96$ customers after the renovation.
